This document contains the step-by-step run through of creating a random forest model. 

# Load Packages and Data 

We will load in pre-defined packages from `packages.R` and read in our data frame `d_samples_global_training.csv` containing 2,635 samples from the longitudinal cohort studies and negative control donor sources. 

```{r}
# Source R packages 
source(here::here("packages.R"))

# Load primary dataset
d <- read.csv(here::here("data/d_samples_global_training.csv")) %>% dplyr::select(-SampleID)
```

# Step 1: Combination Selection 

This code runs all possible combinations from a defined list of proteins and desired number of antigens. 

## Create `fit_models` function to run all combinations

```{r fit_models function}
fit_models <- function(d, N_tree, num_antigens, comb_option, name_of_file) {
    
    d <- d %>%
      dplyr::select(status, all_of(comb_option)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(across(all_of(comb_option), log)) %>%
      na.omit() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(status = as.factor(status))
    
    ### Splitting data into test and train; create folds for cross-validation ####
    set.seed(1234)
    d_folds <- vfold_cv(d, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = status) # creates cross validation
    cores <- parallel::detectCores() -1 # determine number of cores for parallel processing, keep one so you can keep working on computer
    
    # model specification
    rf_model_spec <- rand_forest() %>%
      set_args(trees = N_tree) %>%
      set_engine("ranger", # sets model to random forest using the ranger package
                 importance = "permutation",
                 num.threads = cores, # computes individual random forests in parallel using number of cores in computer
                 seed = 1234) %>% #sets seed
      set_mode("classification")
    
    # Define combinations of predictor variables
    combinations <- combn(comb_option, num_antigens) # creates object with all combinations of 8 antigens in each column
    my_formulas = apply(combinations, 2, 
                        function(x) as.formula(paste("status ~", paste(x, collapse = " + ")))) # creates a list of combinations as a formulas
    
    keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = TRUE)
    rf_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc)
    
    model_fits <- pbapply::pblapply(my_formulas, cl = cores, function(x){
      rf_fit_resamples <- rf_model_spec %>%
        fit_resamples(resamples = d_folds,  control = keep_pred, metrics = rf_metrics, preprocessor = x)
      rf_fit_resamples %>%
        collect_metrics()
    }
    )
    
    numbers <- seq(1, length(my_formulas), 1)
    summary_stats <- sapply(numbers, function(x) {
      as.data.frame(model_fits[[x]]$mean)
    })
    summary_std_err <- sapply(numbers, function(x) {
      as.data.frame(model_fits[[x]]$std_err)
    })
    
    summary_stats_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(as.character(my_formulas), as.numeric(summary_stats), as.numeric(summary_std_err)))
    
    summary_stats_df <- summary_stats_df %>%
      dplyr::rename("formula" = V1) %>%
      dplyr::rename("mean_auc" = V2) %>%
      dplyr::rename("SE" = V3) %>%
      arrange(desc(mean_auc))
    
    fwrite(summary_stats_df, here::here("results/rand_forest/top_combinations/", paste0(name_of_file, "_", num_antigens, "_antigen_summary_stats_df.csv")))
    
    summary_stats_df
    
  }
```

## Run 2-8 antigen combinations 

```{r}
top_10 <- c("EBP","PTEX150","LF005","LF010","RBP2b.P87","LF016","PvCSS","MSP8","s16","LF001")
top_8 <- c("EBP","PTEX150","LF005","LF010","RBP2b.P87","LF016","PvCSS","MSP8")

# To run combinations for between 2 and 8 antigens, use below.
for (i in 2:8) {

  fit_models(
    d, N_tree = 1000, num_antigens = i, comb_option = top_10, name_of_file = "top")

}
```

# Step 2: Hyperparameter tuning

Use the top combination to find the optimal hyperparameter values. This code tunes the hyperparameters of the random forest min_n and mtry. You then use the optimal hyperparameters for final model training in `training_final_model.R`. The format of this code follows that outlined in https://www.tmwr.org. 

## Tuning Steps 

```{r tuning steps}
# 1. Make list of the top proteins, we use this to select columns in the data for model training.
top_combo <- c("EBP", "PTEX150", "PvCSS", "LF005", "LF010", "RBP2b.P87", "LF016", "MSP8")
d <- d %>% dplyr::select(all_of(top_combo), status)

# 2. Splitting data into test and train; create folds for cross-validation
set.seed(1234)
d_folds <- vfold_cv(d, v = 10, strata = status) # creates cross validation
cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1 # determine number of cores, keep 1 so you can work whilst parameter tuning is happening

# Specify and fit model
# Step 1: Define the recipe
rf_all_recipe <- recipe(status ~., data = d) %>%
  step_log(all_predictors()) # logs all the predictor variables

# Step 2: Specify the model
tune_spec <- rand_forest() %>%
  set_args(1000, min_n = tune(), mtry = tune()) %>% # set the tuning parameters
  set_engine(
    "ranger", # sets model to random forest using the ranger package
    importance = "permutation",
    num.threads = cores, # computes individual random forests in parallel using number of cores in computer
    # probability = TRUE,
    seed = 1234
  ) %>% #sets seed
  set_mode("classification")

# Step 3: Define the workflow
tune_workflow <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(rf_all_recipe) %>% 
  add_model(tune_spec) 

# Train the hyperparameters with bayesian optimisation
doParallel::registerDoParallel()

# determine the number of predictor variables / features in your model: This is used to vary the mtry tuning
num_predictors <- length(top_combo) 

rf_param <- tune_workflow %>%
  extract_parameter_set_dials() %>%
  update(mtry = mtry(c(1,num_predictors))) %>%
  update(min_n = min_n(c(1, 40)))

start_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(
  mtry(range = c(1,num_predictors)), # number of randomly drawn candidate variables
  min_n(range = c(1,40)), # number of data points required for split
  size = 50
)

roc_res <- metric_set(roc_auc)

rf_initial <- 
  tune_workflow %>%
  tune_grid(resamples = d_folds, grid = start_grid, metrics = roc_res)

set.seed(456)
rf_bo <- tune_workflow %>%
  tune_bayes(
    resamples = d_folds,
    metrics = roc_res,
    initial = rf_initial,
    objective = exp_improve(), # argument for which acquisition function should be used
    iter = 300,
    control = control_bayes(verbose = T, no_improve = 100),
    param_info = rf_param
  )

show_best(rf_bo)

# Write model and top models
saveRDS(rf_bo, file = here::here("model/hyperparameter_tuning.rds"))
best_hyperparameters <- as.data.frame(show_best(rf_bo))
# fwrite(best_hyperparameters, file = here::here("results/hyperparameter_tuning.csv"))
```

# Step 3A: Training the Final Model

Here we use optimal hyperparameter values to train the model. This code trains the final random forest model on all of the data from the longitudinal cohort studies, as well as the negative controls from Thailand, Brazil and Australia. The model is then saved and used to classify new data as sero-positive/sero-negative. 

Make list of the top proteins to select columns in the data for model training: `All (top_combo) [N=8]`: EBP, PTEX150, PvCSS, LF005, LF010, RBP2b.P87, LF016, MSP8

```{r training final model}
# Make list of the top proteins, we use this to select columns in the data for model training.
top_combo <- c("EBP", "PTEX150", "PvCSS", "LF005", "LF010", "RBP2b.P87", "LF016", "MSP8")
d <- d %>% dplyr::select(all_of(top_combo), status)

# Define hyperparameters and determine number of cores for parallel processing
N_tree <- 10000 # defines number of trees
m_try <- 2 # This number would need to be updated if we redo hyperparameter tuning, e.g. if we use a new combination
min_node <- 7 # This number would need to be updated if we redo hyperparameter tuning, e.g. if we use a new combination
cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1 # determine number of cores

# Specify and fit model
# Step 1: Model Specification
rf_model <- rand_forest() %>%
  set_args(trees = N_tree, mtry = m_try, min_n = min_node) %>%
  set_engine(
    "ranger", # sets model to random forest using the ranger package
    importance = "permutation",
    num.threads = cores, # computes individual random forests in parallel using number of cores in computer
    probability = TRUE,
    seed = 1234
  ) %>% #sets seed
  set_mode("classification")

# Step 2: Define the recipe
rf_all_recipe <- recipe(status ~., data = d) %>%
  step_log(all_predictors()) # logs all the predictor variables

# Step 3: Workflow
antibody_wkfl <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_model) %>%
  add_recipe(rf_all_recipe)

# Step 4: Fit the final model on all the training data (the whole dataset)
final_fit <- fit(antibody_wkfl, data = d)

# Step 5: View
final_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  vip()
# ggsave(here::here("results/importance_antigens.png"), width = 7, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# Step 6: Save the final model
antibody_model <- final_fit
saveRDS(antibody_model, here::here("model/PvSeroTaTmodel.rds"))
```

# Step 3B: Find the Maximised Thresholds 

Use the same hyperparameter values and 10-fold 5-repeat cross-validation. 

## 10-fold 5-repeat cross-validation 

```{r cross-validation step}
# Make list of the top proteins, we use this to select columns in the data for model training.
top_combo <- c("EBP", "PTEX150", "PvCSS", "LF005", "LF010", "RBP2b.P87", "LF016", "MSP8")
d <- d %>% dplyr::select(all_of(top_combo), status)
cores <- parallel::detectCores()

# fit random forest model for each combination
set.seed(1234)
d_folds <- vfold_cv(d, v = 10, repeats = 5, strata = status) # creates cross validation
N_tree <- 10000 # defines number of trees
m_try <-  2
min_n <- 7

# model specification
rf_model <- rand_forest() %>%
  set_args(trees = N_tree, mtry = m_try, min_n = min_n) %>% 
  set_engine("ranger", # sets model to random forest using the ranger package
             importance = "permutation",
             num.threads = cores, # computes individual random forests in parallel using number of cores in computer
             probability = TRUE,
             seed = 1234) %>% #sets seed
  set_mode("classification")

# defines the recipe
rf_all_recipe <- recipe(status ~., data = d) %>%
  step_log(all_predictors()) # logs all the predictor variables

# workflow
antibody_wkfl <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_model) %>%
  add_recipe(rf_all_recipe)

keep_pred <- control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = TRUE)
rf_metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc)

# fit resamples
antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples <- antibody_wkfl %>%
  fit_resamples(resamples = d_folds, control = keep_pred, metrics = rf_metrics)

# collects metrics
antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples %>% collect_metrics()

# collects assessment set predictions: UNSUMARISED 
antibody_wkfl_preds_unsumarised <- antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples %>%
  collect_predictions(summarize = FALSE) 

# plot ROC Curve
antibody_wkfl_preds_unsumarised %>%
  yardstick::roc_curve(truth = status, .pred_new) %>%
  autoplot +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,0.2)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,0.2)) +
  labs(x = "1- Specificity", y = "Sensitivity")

antibody_wkfl_preds_unsumarised %>%
  yardstick::roc_curve(truth = status, .pred_new)

# collects assessment set predictions: SUMARISED 
antibody_wkfl_preds_summarised <- antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples %>%
  collect_predictions(summarize = TRUE) 

results <- d %>%
  dplyr::select(!status) %>%
  cbind(antibody_wkfl_preds_summarised) %>%
  dplyr::select(!c(.row, .config))

RF_ROC <- antibody_wkfl_preds_summarised %>%
  roc_curve(status, .pred_new)

saveRDS(
  antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples,
  here::here("model/antibody_wkfl_fit_resamples.rds")
)
```

## Find sensitivity/specificity thresholds 

```{r find sensitivity and specificity thresholds of interest}
# find the maximised sensitivity/specificity
threshold_max_sens_spec = RF_ROC$.threshold[which.min(abs(RF_ROC$specificity - RF_ROC$sensitivity))]

# find where the random forest votes threshold is above a certain level of sensitivity
RF_ROC_sorted_sens <- RF_ROC %>%
  arrange(desc(.threshold)) # first need to reorder
threshold_85_sens <- RF_ROC_sorted_sens$.threshold[which(RF_ROC_sorted_sens$sensitivity >= 0.85)[1]]
threshold_90_sens <- RF_ROC_sorted_sens$.threshold[which(RF_ROC_sorted_sens$sensitivity >= 0.9)[1]]
threshold_95_sens <- RF_ROC_sorted_sens$.threshold[which(RF_ROC_sorted_sens$sensitivity >= 0.95)[1]]
# find where the random forest votes threshold is above a certain level of specificity
threshold_85_spec <- RF_ROC$.threshold[which(RF_ROC$specificity >= 0.85)[1]]
threshold_90_spec <- RF_ROC$.threshold[which(RF_ROC$specificity >= 0.9)[1]]
threshold_95_spec <- RF_ROC$.threshold[which(RF_ROC$specificity >= 0.95)[1]]

# create a table that can be saved: This table can be input into our code for classifying on new data
threshold_table <- data.frame(
  sens_spec = c("max_sens_spec", "85_sens", "90_sens", "95_sens", "85_spec", "90_spec", "95_spec"),
  threshold = c(threshold_max_sens_spec, threshold_85_sens, threshold_90_sens, threshold_95_sens,
                threshold_85_spec, threshold_90_spec, threshold_95_spec)
)
# write.csv(threshold_table, here::here("results/rand_forest_threshold_values.csv"), row.names = F)
```

# Step 4: Final Trained model: Apply to classify NEW data

- This code reads in the RAU values in the data and classifies rows as sero-positive/sero-negative
- Read in data and change column names formatted for classification
- Put your data into the data folder and read in by amending csv file name
- Select only columns with _Dilution: Often the output from the MAGPIX includes the string _Dilution.
- Some data cleaning may be required to ensure that the column names are as written in the above modelling code!!!! 

`antibody_model`: PvSeroTaTmodel.rds: EBP, PTEX150, PvCSS, LF005, LF010, RBP2b.P87, LF016, MSP8

```{r}
d <- read.csv(here::here("data/d_samples_global_training.csv")) 

# Reads in serostatus using the trained random forest
antibody_model <- readRDS(here::here("model/PvSeroTaTmodel.rds"))

# function to 
classify_final_results <- function(data, algorithm_type, Sens_Spec, file_name) {
  # Read in the random forest votes threshold values
  threshold_table <- if(algorithm_type == "antibody_model"){
    read.csv(here::here("model/threshold_values.csv"))
  } else {
    stop("Invalid model provided")
  }
  # Determine random forest votes threshold based on the algorithm_type string
  threshold <- if (Sens_Spec == "maximised") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "max_sens_spec") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "85% sensitivity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "85_sens") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "90% sensitivity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "90_sens") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "95% sensitivity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "95_sens") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "85% specificity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "85_spec") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "90% specificity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "90_spec") %>% pull(threshold)
  } else if (Sens_Spec == "95% specificity") {
    threshold_table %>% filter(sens_spec == "95_spec") %>% pull(threshold)
  }
  else {
    stop("Invalid sensitivity/specificity type provided.")
  }
  # Retrieve the model based on the algorithm_type string
  model <- get(algorithm_type)
  # Classify data using the specified model
  class_preds <- predict(model, new_data = data)
  prob_preds <- predict(model, new_data = data, type = "prob")
  # Binds predictions to data
  results <- data %>%
    bind_cols(class_preds, prob_preds)
  
  # Classify new (seropositive) / old (seronegative) based on selected threshold
  results <- results %>%
    mutate(pred_class_max = ifelse(.pred_new > threshold, "new", "old")) %>%
    mutate(pred_class_max = as.factor(pred_class_max))
  
  # Final processing and renaming
  final_results <- results %>%
    select(-c(.pred_class, .pred_new, .pred_old)) %>%
    mutate(pred_class_max = recode(pred_class_max, "new" = "seropositive", "old" = "seronegative"))
  
  # Save results to CSV
  fwrite(final_results, here::here(paste0("results/", file_name, "_results.csv")))
  
  # Return the table of prediction classes
  return(final_results)
}

# run function by specifying your dataframe and which algorithm you want to use
test <- classify_final_results(
  # specify which data you want to classify
  data = d, 
  # Select which model you want to run. This needs to be a character string.
  # antibody_model is for the 8-antigen combination. 
  algorithm_type = "antibody_model", 
  # select the sensitivity/specificity that you are interested in.
  # This must be a character string and can either be maximised, 85% sensitivity, 90% sensitivity, 95% sensitivity
  # or 85% specificity, 90% specificity, 95% specificity
  Sens_Spec = "maximised",
  # Specify file name for saving purposes
  file_name = "testing")
# investigate the classifications
table(test$pred_class_max)

write.csv(test, "results/longitudinal_results_processed.csv")
```
